story-overview.user-story: As a user, I want to create and manage triggers through conversation with Annie, so that I can set up proactive reminders and alerts naturally.
story-overview.description:
This story implements the MCP tools that enable the LLM to create and manage proactive triggers during conversation. These tools call the backend IntentsClient which communicates with agentic-memories service for trigger persistence.
The tools are designed to teach the LLM when and how to use proactive features through comprehensive descriptions and schema documentation.

criterion.name: create_trigger Tool
criterion.requirements: - Full schema as defined in Design Doc Section 5.1 - Comprehensive description teaching LLM when to use (reminders, alerts, check-ins) - Cron expression examples in description - How to write rich action_context - Returns created trigger with ID and next_check

criterion.name: list_triggers Tool
criterion.requirements: - Filter by trigger_type: cron, interval, once, price, silence, portfolio, or all - Option to include disabled triggers - Returns array with: id, intent_name, schedule/condition, enabled, next_check, execution_count

criterion.name: update_trigger Tool
criterion.requirements: - Accepts trigger_id + partial updates - Can modify schedule, condition, action_context, enabled - Description explains pause vs delete difference

criterion.name: delete_trigger Tool
criterion.requirements: - Requires trigger_id + confirm=true - Description emphasizes confirmation with user first - Returns success confirmation

criterion.name: Tool Execution
criterion.requirements: - Tool calls IntentsClient (backend HTTP client to agentic-memories) - User ID extracted from session context - Returns structured success/failure - Errors include clear messages for LLM

design-reference.architecture-doc:
See: /Users/ankit/dev/annie/docs/design/proactive-ai-architecture.md
Key sections: - Section 3: Trigger Types (scheduled vs condition) - Section 4: Action Context Specification - Section 5: MCP Tool Definitions (complete schemas) - Section 11: Examples (user interactions)

type.name: scheduled
type.description: Fire at specific times via cron or one-time datetime
type.modes: - cron: Recurring schedule with cron expression - once: One-time execution at specific datetime
type.examples: - "Every morning at 9am" → cron: "0 9 * * *" - "Every weekday at 8:30" → cron: "30 8 * * 1-5" - "Every Friday at 5pm" → cron: "0 17 * * 5" - "Remind me tomorrow at 3pm" → once mode

type.name: condition
type.condition-types: - price: Stock price threshold (e.g., "NVDA < 130") - portfolio: Portfolio metric (e.g., "any_holding_change > 5%") - silence: User inactivity (e.g., "inactive_hours > 48")
type.parameters: - expression: Human-readable condition - check_interval_minutes: How often to evaluate (default: 5) - cooldown_hours: Min hours between fires (default: 24) - fire_mode: "once" or "recurring" (default: recurring)

action-context-specification.description: Rich briefing document written by creation LLM for wake-up LLM. Contains everything needed to execute the trigger properly.

required-sections.section: Preserve user's exact words for ground truth
1-3 sentence distillation of what trigger should accomplish
CRITICAL: Only invariant data (name, timezone, communication style). NEVER snapshot dynamic data (portfolio holdings, prices). Wake-up LLM must fetch fresh data via tools.
Step-by-step guide: 1. GATHER DATA (which tools to call) 2. EVALUATE WHETHER TO SEND (skip conditions) 3. COMPOSE MESSAGE (tone, length, content) 4. ERROR HANDLING (what if data unavailable)
- Tone (casual/professional/enthusiastic) - Length (brief/moderate/detailed) - Formatting preferences - What to emphasize/de-emphasize
List which tools wake-up agent should use
How to handle missing data, empty results, errors

tool-registration.description: Tools are registered in mcp_server/server.py via MCPServer.register_default_tools()
tool-registration.example-from-server-py: def register_default_tools(self): """Register default tools.""" self.tool_registry.register(health_check_tool) self.tool_registry.register(store_memory_tool) self.tool_registry.register(retrieve_memories_tool) self.tool_registry.register(get_user_profile_tool) # Portfolio management tools self.tool_registry.register(get_portfolio_tool) self.tool_registry.register(add_holding_tool) # ... etc

tool-definition-structure.description: Tools are defined as dictionaries with name, description, inputSchema, and handler. Stored in mcp_server/tools.py.

async-handler-pattern.description: Tool handlers can be async functions. Server auto-detects and awaits if needed.

http-client-pattern.description: MCP tools call backend/external services via httpx.AsyncClient. Pattern: async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=X) as client
http-client-pattern.best-practices: - Use async with for automatic cleanup - Set appropriate timeouts (5-10s for reads, 180s for LLM operations) - Handle all HTTP error codes gracefully - Return structured {"status": "success"|"error", ...} responses - Log all operations with structured logging - Include duration_ms in logs for performance tracking

error-handling-pattern.description: Tools should handle errors gracefully and return LLM-friendly messages.

intents-client-location.description: HTTP client for calling agentic-memories intents endpoints. Similar pattern to MemoryClient and existing HTTP clients.

client-pattern-reference.description: Follow the pattern established in backend/api/memory_client.py
client-pattern-reference.structure:
class IntentsClient: """Async HTTP client for agentic-memories intents service."""
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 10.0
def __init__(self, memories_url: Optional[str] = None): # Load from config or use default config = get_config() self.memories_url = memories_url or config.get("AGENTIC_MEMORIES_URL") self.client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=self.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)
async def create_intent(self, user_id: str, intent_data: dict) -> dict: """Create a new intent/trigger.""" url = f"{self.memories_url}/v1/intents" response = await self.client.post(url, json=intent_data) # ... handle response
async def list_intents(self, user_id: str, filters: dict = None) -> dict: """List user's intents.""" url = f"{self.memories_url}/v1/intents" response = await self.client.get(url, params={"user_id": user_id, ...}) # ... handle response
async def update_intent(self, intent_id: str, updates: dict) -> dict: """Update existing intent.""" url = f"{self.memories_url}/v1/intents/{intent_id}" response = await self.client.put(url, json=updates) # ... handle response
async def delete_intent(self, intent_id: str, user_id: str) -> dict: """Delete intent.""" url = f"{self.memories_url}/v1/intents/{intent_id}" response = await self.client.delete(url, params={"user_id": user_id}) # ... handle response

mcp-to-backend-flow.description: MCP tool handler calls IntentsClient, which calls agentic-memories HTTP API
mcp-to-backend-flow.flow:
1. LLM calls MCP tool: create_trigger(user_id, intent_name, trigger_type, ...) 2. MCP tool handler (in mcp_server/tools.py): - Import IntentsClient (needs to be accessible from MCP server) - PROBLEM: IntentsClient is in backend/, MCP server is separate service - SOLUTION: MCP tools call backend API endpoint, which uses IntentsClient
Revised flow: 1. LLM calls MCP tool: create_trigger(...) 2. MCP tool handler makes HTTP call to backend endpoint 3. Backend endpoint (backend/api/routes/intents.py) uses IntentsClient 4. IntentsClient calls agentic-memories 5. Response flows back to MCP tool → LLM
Alternative (simpler for Story 13.2): 1. MCP tool handler directly calls agentic-memories intents API 2. No backend intermediary needed 3. Similar to how store_memory_tool works currently

recommended-approach.description:
For Story 13.2: MCP tools call agentic-memories intents API directly via HTTP. This matches the pattern used by store_memory_tool and get_portfolio_tool.
No need for IntentsClient abstraction in MCP tools. Backend can create its own IntentsClient later if needed for other features.
recommended-approach.rationale: - Simpler: One less abstraction layer - Consistent: Matches existing MCP tool patterns - Faster: Direct communication, no backend hop - Tools already make HTTP calls to agentic-memories

tool-descriptions-guidance.importance: Tool descriptions are CRITICAL. They teach the LLM when and how to use proactive features. The description is the LLM's primary instruction manual for the tool.

description-structure.section: Signal phrases and user intent patterns
Common use cases with concrete examples

tool-descriptions-guidance.example-good-description:
"description": """ Create a proactive trigger that will cause Annie to initiate contact with the user.
USE THIS WHEN USER WANTS: - Reminders: "Remind me to...", "Every morning tell me...", "On Friday..." - Alerts: "Let me know when NVDA drops below $130", "Alert me if any stock moves 5%" - Check-ins: "If I don't message you for 2 days, check in", "Ping me if I'm silent" - Scheduled updates: "Every weekday, give me a portfolio summary"
CRON EXPRESSIONS (for scheduled triggers): - "every morning at 9am" → "0 9 * * *" - "every weekday at 8:30" → "30 8 * * 1-5" - "every Friday at 5pm" → "0 17 * * 5" - "twice a day (9am and 5pm)" → "0 9,17 * * *"
ACTION_CONTEXT GUIDANCE: Write a comprehensive briefing for the wake-up AI that includes: 1. original_request: User's exact words 2. intent_summary: What this trigger should accomplish (1-3 sentences) 3. user_context: Name, timezone, communication preferences (NOT dynamic data like holdings) 4. execution_instructions: Step-by-step guide for wake-up AI 5. message_guidance: Tone, length, formatting preferences 6. edge_cases: How to handle errors or missing data
IMPORTANT: - NEVER put dynamic data (portfolio holdings, prices) in action_context - execution_instructions MUST say "Retrieve current portfolio/profile first" - Be thorough - this briefing is everything the wake-up AI knows """
